cve_summary: Integer overflow in the index.c:read_entry() function while decompressing a compressed prefix length in libgit2 before v0.26.2 allows an attacker to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) via a crafted repository index file.
commit_message:
index: error out on unreasonable prefix-compressed path lengths

When computing the complete path length from the encoded
prefix-compressed path, we end up just allocating the complete path
without ever checking what the encoded path length actually is. This can
easily lead to a denial of service by just encoding an unreasonable long
path name inside of the index. Git already enforces a maximum path
length of 4096 bytes. As we also have that enforcement ready in some
places, just make sure that the resulting path is smaller than
GIT_PATH_MAX.

Reported-by: Krishna Ram Prakash R <krp@gtux.in>
Reported-by: Vivek Parikh <viv0411.parikh@gmail.com>
docstring:
"""
Summary: 
Reads an index entry from a buffer and populates the provided output parameters.

Parameters: 
out (git_index_entry **): Pointer to store the resulting index entry.
out_size (size_t *): Pointer to store the size of the entry read.
index (git_index *): The index from which to read the entry.
buffer (const void *): The buffer containing the index entry data.
buffer_size (size_t): The size of the buffer.
last (const char *): The last part of the path to reconstruct the full path.

Returns: 
int: Returns 0 on success, or -1 on failure.

Logic: 
The function checks if the buffer is large enough to contain an index entry. It then reads the entry data from the buffer, handling both compressed and uncompressed paths. It allocates memory for the path if necessary and populates the output parameters with the entry details. Finally, it checks for errors and returns the appropriate status.
